preconditions: One binary input is controlled by a lever.
A solid input attachment block and a redstone wall torch are available.
The output can be reached by a legal redstone path without an input-to-output bypass.
logicalIdentity: A redstone torch emits the inverse of the powered state of its attachment block.
requiredConnections: The input lever directly controls the shared input attachment block.

The inverter wall torch hangs on that exact same input attachment block (its facing points away from that block). Alternatively the torch may hang on any block that a wire line from the lever ends inside of or lies on top of; a wire passing beside the block is not enough.
The first output-route receiver is face-adjacent to the inverter torch, on any side except the attachment side.
The output route physically delivers power to the output lamp: the last wire's line points into the lamp or lies on top of it.
No block that the lever powers (the lever itself, its attachment block) is face-adjacent to the output lamp.
physicalInvariants: Input A=0 leaves the attachment block unpowered, so the torch and output are on.
Input A=1 powers the attachment block, so the torch and output are off.
The lever or its directly powered attachment block does not power the lamp through a bypass.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the input reaches a separate torch support only through a wire running alongside it
invalidPatterns.reason: A wire powers only the block it ends in or lies on; the support stays unpowered and the torch never turns off.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the first output receiver is diagonal from the torch
invalidPatterns.reason: The inverter output path is physically disconnected.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the torch attachment block touches the output lamp
invalidPatterns.reason: When A=1 that block is powered and lights the lamp directly, so Y=1 instead of 0.

preconditions: Two binary inputs are controlled independently.
The allowed blocks can construct two input inverters, a redstone merge network, one output inverter, and an output route.
The workspace has enough separation to prevent direct input-to-output bypasses.
logicalIdentity: A AND B = NOT((NOT A) OR (NOT B)).
roles: merge network carrying (NOT A) OR (NOT B)
solid attachment block controlled by the merge network
requiredConnections: Input A directly controls the attachment block of the A inverter.
Input B directly controls the attachment block of the B inverter.
Each input inverter has a merge-network wire face-adjacent to it at the SAME height (a wire one level lower or higher and one block sideways is diagonal and receives nothing).
Both input-inverter outputs physically connect to one continuous merge network.
The merge network powers the exact attachment block of the final inverter: a merge wire ends its line inside that block or lies on top of it.
The final inverter hangs on that attachment block, not on the output lamp, and has a wire or the lamp face-adjacent to it on a free side.
The output route physically delivers power to the output lamp.
physicalInvariants: When either input is 0, at least one input inverter is on, the merge network is powered, and the final inverter is off.
Only when A=1 and B=1 are both input inverters off, leaving the final-inverter attachment unpowered and the output on.
Every inverter reacts to its actual attachment block rather than to a merely nearby signal.
All four input combinations have a combinational, history-independent output.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the two input-inverter outputs are described as merged but their wires are not physically continuous
invalidPatterns.reason: The logical OR of the inverted inputs is not constructed.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the final torch is beside the merge wire but its attachment block is not powered by that wire
invalidPatterns.reason: A torch inverts only its attachment block; a wire running past the block does not power it.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the merge wire runs one level above or below the input torches
invalidPatterns.reason: Each torch is diagonal to the wire, so the merge network never receives the inverted inputs and the output is constant.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the final inverter hangs on the output lamp
invalidPatterns.reason: A torch never powers its own attachment block, so the lamp can never light.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the final inverter and lamp touch only diagonally
invalidPatterns.reason: The output is physically disconnected.

preconditions: Two independently routed binary source nets are available.
Repeaters and redstone wire are allowed when either source must remain isolated from the merged net.
The merge can reach its consumer without touching an unrelated input or output lane.
logicalIdentity: A redstone merge is powered when either isolated incoming branch is powered.
roles: one directional repeater per incoming branch
requiredConnections: Each source route reaches the input side of its own repeater; repeater facing names that input side in the layout contract.
The output side of each repeater reaches a different coordinate on one physically continuous merge wire.
No merge-wire coordinate touches either source route on the source side of its repeater, so the merged net cannot back-power or join the inputs.
The merge wire ends straight into the output consumer, lies on top of its attachment block, or feeds the input side of a final repeater that points at the consumer.
If more than fifteen wire steps occur between powered components, an outward-facing repeater refreshes the signal before it reaches zero.
physicalInvariants: A=0 and B=0 leave every merge coordinate unpowered.
A=1 or B=1 powers the merge and its consumer.
The two inputs remain distinct nets until after their isolation repeaters.
A neighbouring wire that merely runs past a solid consumer does not count as delivery unless its line points into that consumer.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the two source wires are joined before their branch repeaters
invalidPatterns.reason: The inputs become one net and can power each other's inverter attachment blocks.

invalidPatterns.pattern: both repeaters point away from their sources
invalidPatterns.reason: A repeater is directional; neither incoming signal reaches the merge.

invalidPatterns.pattern: two intended independent lanes are in adjacent horizontal coordinates for several blocks
invalidPatterns.reason: Redstone wire joins side-to-side and silently creates an unintended OR before the intended gate.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the last merge wire turns beside the consumer instead of ending into it
invalidPatterns.reason: The powered wire can run alongside the consumer without delivering power.

preconditions: Original A and B nets can each fan out through isolated routes to one NOR stage and one AND stage.
A verified two-input AND implementation, one direct NOR attachment and one final inverter are available.
The workspace can keep the NOR input merge, AND network and final two-source merge from touching accidentally.
logicalIdentity: A XOR B = NOT(NOR(A,B) OR (A AND B)).
roles: NOR attachment block fed by A OR B
final attachment block fed by NOR(A,B) OR AND(A,B)
requiredConnections: Route isolated copies of original A and B onto one continuous input merge that actually powers the NOR attachment block; the wall torch on that block emits NOR(A,B).
Route separate isolated copies of A and B through the verified De Morgan AND implementation to produce A AND B.
Keep the NOR output route and AND output route physically separate until they reach two different sides of the final attachment block.
The NOR output and AND output must each actually power the final attachment block by a straight wire endpoint, wire on top, or repeater output; a wire passing beside it is insufficient.
The final wall torch hangs on that exact final attachment block and has a face-adjacent receiver on a free side leading to Y.
If the AND signal is also needed as a carry output, branch it through a directional repeater before the final XOR attachment so the two consumers cannot back-power each other.
physicalInvariants: For A=0,B=0, NOR=1 and AND=0, so the final attachment is powered and Y=0.
For A=1,B=0 or A=0,B=1, NOR=0 and AND=0, so the final attachment is unpowered and Y=1.
For A=1,B=1, NOR=0 and AND=1, so the final attachment is powered and Y=0.
The NOR and AND outputs remain distinct until the final attachment block, and neither touches the final torch's output route.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the NOR and AND routes merge into ordinary wire before reaching the final attachment
invalidPatterns.reason: The merged signal can back-power either subcircuit; isolate branches or terminate them independently at the final block.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the NOR input wire passes beside its attachment block and then turns away
invalidPatterns.reason: The NOR block is never powered, so its torch stays lit in every row.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the final attachment is omitted and the NOR and AND wires merely run beside the final torch
invalidPatterns.reason: A torch only inverts its attachment block, not nearby dust.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the final attachment block or either of its input routes touches the output lamp
invalidPatterns.reason: A powered input to the final inverter can bypass the torch and light the lamp in rows where XOR must be zero.

logicalFunction: SUM = A XOR B; CARRY = A AND B
preconditions: Two binary inputs drive both a sum and a carry output.
The allowed blocks support the verified AND implementation, direct NOR and final XOR inverter.
The carry net can fan out once through directional isolation.
logicalIdentity: CARRY = A AND B; SUM = NOT(NOR(A,B) OR CARRY).
roles: A OR B input merge followed by a NOR torch
final SUM attachment fed by the NOR and shared carry
final SUM torch and output route
requiredConnections: Build one A AND B signal using the verified De Morgan AND implementation; do not build a second copy for SUM.
Branch the AND output through one directional route to CARRY and through a separately isolated route to one side of the SUM attachment block.
Route isolated original A and B branches into one NOR attachment; route its wall-torch output to a different side of the SUM attachment block.
Both the NOR route and carry route must actually power the SUM attachment block without becoming adjacent anywhere upstream.
The SUM wall torch hangs on that attachment block and powers only the SUM delivery route; the carry delivery route must not touch the SUM lamp.
physicalInvariants: At 00, NOR alone powers the SUM attachment, so SUM=0 and CARRY=0.
At 01 and 10, neither NOR nor CARRY powers the SUM attachment, so SUM=1 and CARRY=0.
At 11, CARRY alone powers the SUM attachment, so SUM=0 and CARRY=1.
The same physical AND signal is observed by CARRY and used as one input of the SUM inverter.

invalidPatterns.pattern: SUM is built as a separate large dual-rail XOR while an AND signal already exists
invalidPatterns.reason: The extra gates and fanout add unnecessary collision and cross-talk risks; reuse the verified shared identity.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the carry branch and NOR branch join as wire before the SUM attachment
invalidPatterns.reason: They can back-power their source networks instead of acting as isolated inputs to the final inverter.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the carry delivery wire runs beside the SUM lamp
invalidPatterns.reason: CARRY=1 can light SUM directly and bypass XOR inversion.

logicalFunction: SUM = A XOR B XOR CIN; COUT = majority(A,B,CIN)
preconditions: Three binary inputs require odd parity and majority outputs, including a conventional full adder or equivalent majority/parity circuit.
Two half-adder stages can occupy separate routing bands.
The two carry terms can enter an isolated OR merge.
logicalIdentity: X=A XOR B; C1=A AND B; SUM=X XOR CIN; C2=X AND CIN; COUT=C1 OR C2. This COUT equals majority(A,B,CIN).
roles: first verified half-adder for A and B
second verified half-adder for X and CIN
requiredConnections: Lay out the first half-adder in one band, producing physically separate X and C1 routes.
Feed X through directional fanout into both inputs that need it in the second half-adder; do not run X alongside C1.
Lay out the second half-adder in a separate band, using X and original CIN to produce SUM and C2.
Feed C1 and C2 through separate repeaters into the isolated OR merge for COUT; neither carry route may touch SUM or an XOR attachment block.
Keep the final SUM and COUT delivery lanes separated through their fixed lamp coordinates.

For a LogicDesign expressed as three pairwise AND terms, the same physical COUT is valid because (A AND B) OR ((A XOR B) AND CIN) is Boolean-equivalent to the three-term majority equation; map all active node and edge IDs to the blocks that realize their equivalent signal.
physicalInvariants: The first half-adder's X output matches A XOR B for all four A,B combinations before CIN is considered.
The second half-adder produces SUM=X XOR CIN and C2=X AND CIN.
C1 and C2 are mutually exclusive, so their isolated OR is COUT without feedback.
Across all eight rows, SUM is odd parity and COUT is one exactly when at least two inputs are one.

invalidPatterns.pattern: three separate pairwise AND circuits are packed beside a separate two-stage XOR
invalidPatterns.reason: This duplicates fanout and creates many adjacent nets; the two-half-adder factorization uses fewer shared physical signals.

invalidPatterns.pattern: X and C1 share adjacent dust after the first half-adder
invalidPatterns.reason: The intermediate parity and carry become one net, corrupting both second-stage inputs.

invalidPatterns.pattern: C1 or C2 joins the COUT merge before an isolation repeater
invalidPatterns.reason: The merge can feed backward into a half-adder and hold a gate attachment powered.

invalidPatterns.pattern: the two half-adders reuse one attachment block
invalidPatterns.reason: One stage then switches torches in the other stage and the composition is no longer acyclic.

logicalFunction: Acyclic composition of multiple NOT, AND, OR, XOR, and XNOR stages
preconditions: A checked acyclic LogicDesign contains more than one physical gate or an input fans out to several consumers.
The workspace permits separated routing lanes or supported vertical crossings.
Repeaters are available for directional isolation and signal refresh.
logicalIdentity: A correct gate composition preserves each intermediate Boolean net as a distinct physical redstone net until an explicit logical merge.
roles: one spatial lane per intermediate net
requiredConnections: Assign every intermediate signal a lane before placing blocks; unrelated horizontal wire lanes must have at least one unused coordinate between them.
Place a repeater at the start of each branch when one signal fans out, with its input side touching only the source net and its output side touching only that branch.
A gate input branch must end into its attachment block through a straight wire endpoint, a wire on top, or a repeater output pointing into the block.
For a crossing, raise one route on explicit solid supports so no wire can climb or descend into the other; audit every face and step adjacency at both ends of the bridge.
Keep distinct output routes separated through their lamps so one powered output cannot light or join the other output's delivery block.
After placement, trace every truth-table row through actual torch attachment states and repeater directions, not through implements labels.
physicalInvariants: No pair of physically adjacent redstone wires belongs to unrelated logic nets.
Every wall torch has exactly one intended solid attachment block and at least one free-side output receiver.
Every route longer than fifteen wire coordinates is refreshed before power decays to zero.
Changing one input can affect only branches reachable through the directed physical topology.
A lamp is powered only by its own final output net.

invalidPatterns.pattern: parallel buses are packed into consecutive rows or columns
invalidPatterns.reason: Redstone dust connects sideways, joining inputs and intermediate nets into one circuit.

invalidPatterns.pattern: a branch repeater is omitted because the implements IDs differ
invalidPatterns.reason: Implements metadata never provides electrical isolation; only physical geometry and directional components do.

invalidPatterns.pattern: a vertical bridge has redstone wire on adjacent stair-step levels
invalidPatterns.reason: Dust can climb the step and connect the crossing nets.

invalidPatterns.pattern: several gates share one attachment block merely to save space
invalidPatterns.reason: Power intended for any one gate switches every torch attached to that block.
